headline: Banglamotor chaos: Expelled Jubo Dal leader detained after man injured
summary: Ferdous Ahmed Simon was taken into custody around midnight after an altercation left a man injured and sparked protests by locals over extortion allegations.
details: A 45-year-old man was injured during an altercation with Ferdous Ahmed Simon, an expelled convener of Hatirjheel Thana Jubo Dal, in Dhaka’s Banglamotor on Thursday night.

According to Hatirjheel Police Station OC Md Asaduzzaman, Simon and the victim, Sohan, are neighbors who became involved in an argument. Sohan was struck on the head, and it is alleged that Simon fired two blank rounds at the scene.
The incident sparked tension, with over 100 locals gathering outside Simon’s home to chant slogans and accuse him of long-term extortion in the neighborhood.
Chaos escalated as a motorcycle was seen on fire beside the Banglamotor-Moghbazar road, requiring the intervention of the Fire Service.
Some locals alleged that law enforcement was initially protecting Simon instead of detaining him, leading to further friction.
Police eventually escorted Simon out of his residence and took him into custody around midnight. Legal proceedings are currently underway.
caption:
An expelled Jubo Dal leader was detained after a late-night altercation in Banglamotor left a man injured and sparked local protests.

A 45-year-old man was injured during an altercation with Ferdous Ahmed Simon, an expelled convener of Hatirjheel Thana Jubo Dal, in Dhaka’s Banglamotor on Thursday night.

According to Hatirjheel Police Station OC Md Asaduzzaman, Simon and the victim, Sohan, are neighbors who became involved in an argument. Sohan was struck on the head, and it is alleged that Simon fired two blank rounds at the scene.

The incident sparked tension, with over 100 locals gathering outside Simon’s home to chant slogans and accuse him of long-term extortion in the neighborhood.

Chaos escalated as a motorcycle was seen on fire beside the Banglamotor-Moghbazar road, requiring the intervention of the Fire Service.

Some locals alleged that law enforcement was initially protecting Simon instead of detaining him, leading to further friction.

Police eventually escorted Simon out of his residence and took him into custody around midnight. Legal proceedings are currently underway.

headline_marked: BRUR [[sacks 11 staff including 3 teachers]] over Abu Sayed killing
headline: BRUR sacks 11 staff including 3 teachers over Abu Sayed killing
summary: Begum Rokeya University Rangpur (BRUR) permanently terminated the employment of 11 staff members following an International Crimes Tribunal order.
details: Begum Rokeya University Rangpur (BRUR) has sacked 11 staff members, including three teachers, for their involvement in the killing of Abu Sayed during the July 2024 Anti-discrimination Student Movement.
The decision was made during the university's 123rd syndicate meeting on Wednesday, following an order issued by the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT).
Abu Sayed, an English department student, was shot and killed by police outside the university gate on July 16, 2024, during quota reform protests.
The dismissed teachers include Associate Prof Asaduzzaman Mandal Asad, Associate Prof Mashiur Rahman, and Associate Prof Shariful Islam, the university's former proctor.
Among the administrative staff sacked are former assistant registrars Rafiul Hasan Russell and Hafizur Rahman Tufan, and several others including security guards and office assistants.
Vice-Chancellor Prof Md Showkat Ali stated that the university acted on an ICT order received two days prior to the syndicate meeting.
In a separate ICT-2 verdict on April 9, former police officers were sentenced to death, while others received life sentences or prison terms.
Former vice-chancellor Hasibur Rashid and two absconding teachers were among those sentenced in absentia to 10 years in prison.
caption:
11 university staff and teachers sacked. The fallout from the killing of Abu Sayed continues.

Begum Rokeya University Rangpur (BRUR) has sacked 11 staff members, including three teachers, for their involvement in the killing of Abu Sayed during the July 2024 Anti-discrimination Student Movement.

The decision was made during the university's 123rd syndicate meeting on Wednesday, following an order issued by the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT).

Abu Sayed, an English department student, was shot and killed by police outside the university gate on July 16, 2024, during quota reform protests.

The dismissed teachers include Associate Prof Asaduzzaman Mandal Asad, Associate Prof Mashiur Rahman, and Associate Prof Shariful Islam, the university's former proctor.

Among the administrative staff sacked are former assistant registrars Rafiul Hasan Russell and Hafizur Rahman Tufan, and several others including security guards and office assistants.

Vice-Chancellor Prof Md Showkat Ali stated that the university acted on an ICT order received two days prior to the syndicate meeting.

In a separate ICT-2 verdict on April 9, former police officers were sentenced to death, while others received life sentences or prison terms.

Former vice-chancellor Hasibur Rashid and two absconding teachers were among those sentenced in absentia to 10 years in prison.
